intro: You are at Anadoluhisarı, a castle and walls in İstanbul province, from 1394. Bayezid I raised this fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus. Sixty years later, Rumeli Hisarı went up opposite, and the strait was closed completely.
history: In 1394, while preparing to besiege Constantinople, Bayezid I raised this fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, at the mouth of the Göksu. Sixty years later, Mehmed II built Rumeli Hisarı on the opposite shore. From then on, every ship passing the strait was caught between the guns of the two castles.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the keep and the curtain walls. Look out to the mouth of the Göksu, and stroll through the village inside the walls.
facts: Did you know? There are still houses inside the fortress: the quarter that grew between its walls stayed on after the castle's military life ended. The fortress went up in 1394; sixty years later Rumeli Hisarı rose opposite, and every ship in the strait was caught between the two.
outro: This brings our tour of Anadoluhisarı to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls have guarded the strait for centuries; let them keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
